findings.issue_text: [BUG] I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is invoked only in ApplicationController#set_locale, so any context that sets I18n.locale outside the request cycle (Sidekiq jobs, mailers, serializers) never preloads the fallback locales that FallbackLocaleList#[] promises (user locale → SiteSetting.default_locale → :en). In a background job or system-generated email for a user whose locale is missing a key, TranslateAccelerator only loads config.locale; I18n::Backend::Fallbacks then calls super for each fallback locale, and unloaded locales return nil and are silently skipped — so a site whose default_locale is, say, 'de' renders fallback text in English instead of German for every email and queued job, diverging from the fallback order the initializer defines for web requests.

[ADVISORY] The new behavior-bearing logic in this diff — FallbackLocaleList#[] (custom fallback chain), FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!, I18n.ensure_loaded! in translate_accelerator.rb, and the initializer wiring — ships with no test coverage anywhere in the diff (no spec/, test/, or *.spec.* files are touched). Any regression in the fallback chain (e.g. the ensure_loaded! dedupe, the SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym ordering, or the Hash subclass contract expected by I18n::Backend::Fallbacks) fails silently in production rendering with no failing spec to catch it; a follow-up change to the chain order or the loaded-locales bookkeeping has nothing to verify against.

[ADVISORY] The new fallback chain [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en] silently drops the language-root hop that the removed config.i18n.fallbacks = true provided via I18n::Locale::Fallbacks (e.g. pt_BR → pt → …), so region-variant locales no longer fall back to their parent language unless it happens to be the site default. A site with default_locale 'en' and a user on a region variant such as 'pt_BR' or 'zh_TW' now gets the English string for any key missing in the region variant, where the pre-diff configuration returned the parent language ('pt'/'zh') translation — a silent regression for every non-default region locale the TODO comment only defers rather than addresses.

[ADVISORY] The initializer enables fallbacks unconditionally for every environment, whereas the deleted lines show fallbacks were previously enabled only in production.rb, profile.rb, and cloud66/production.rb — development and test environments now also resolve missing keys through the fallback chain. Developers no longer see 'translation missing' placeholders for keys absent from a non-English locale (they see the English text instead), and any spec that asserts a missing-translation error/string for an unloaded locale now silently resolves via fallback, masking missing-translation regressions instead of surfacing them.

[BUG] The fallback-chain preloading invariant introduced by this PR (every locale in [user locale, site default, :en] must be loaded before lookup) is enforced only in ApplicationController#set_locale, leaving every non-request execution path unguarded. Background jobs and mailers (e.g. notification emails rendered on a Sidekiq worker for a zh_CN user) set I18n.locale without ever calling I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!; the accelerator's translate only loads config.locale (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb line 68), so the site-default and :en fallback locales in the chain produced by FallbackLocaleList#[] are not loaded in that process, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks' lookups on them return nil, and emails/jobs emit raw 'translation missing: en.key' strings. The PR's own mechanism (ensure_loaded! added at lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb lines 62-65) exists precisely to make the whole chain loaded, but it is wired into exactly one call site, so the feature it advertises does not hold for the most translation-sensitive server-side path (email).

[ADVISORY] The new fallback-orchestration logic (FallbackLocaleList#[] fallback ordering, its uniq/compact edge behavior, and TranslateAccelerator#ensure_loaded!) ships with zero test coverage anywhere in this diff. Any regression in the fallback order — e.g. the chain collapsing when the requested locale equals the site default or :en, or SiteSetting.default_locale being read at the wrong time — silently changes which translation every user of a non-English site sees, and nothing in CI would catch it; this is new behavior-bearing logic (a custom fallbacks class replacing Rails' config.i18n.fallbacks in production, profile, and cloud66 environments) with no spec exercising even the happy path.

[BUG] The initializer unconditionally enables I18n fallbacks in every environment, silently expanding the stated objective from 'production fallbacks' (the removed config.i18n.fallbacks = true existed only in production/cloud66/profile) to 'fallbacks in development and test too' — a scope change made in code with no explicit acceptance. Test suites that assert missing translations raise I18n::MissingTranslation now silently pass because lookups resolve through the fallback chain to :en; developers running development mode get English fallback text instead of visible missing-translation markers, masking untranslated-key regressions.

[BUG] The custom FallbackLocaleList#[] chain [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en] drops the parent-locale fallback (e.g. zh-TW→zh, pt-BR→pt) that the removed config.i18n.fallbacks = true provided via I18n::Locale::Fallbacks#[] (which prepends locale parents), silently regressing previously-shipped production behavior beyond the PR's stated intent of adding site-locale fallbacks. Users on region-specific locales that Discourse only partially translates (zh_TW, zh_CN, pt_BR) stop receiving the parent-language translation they got before this change and fall straight to English; the in-diff TODO comment confirms the author knows the parent chain is missing but the regression to existing production behavior was not called out as a trade-off.

[ADVISORY] I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is wired only into ApplicationController#set_locale, so the fallback-chain preloading covers only the web-controller happy path; every other translate context (mailers, background jobs) translates without ensuring the chain locales are loaded. The first email or Sidekiq job rendered in a user locale whose fallback locales are not yet loaded can hit I18n::MissingTranslation for keys the web path serves fine — an inconsistency that only manifests outside the request cycle and will be attributed to the fallbacks feature.

[ADVISORY] The unconditional `require 'i18n/backend/fallbacks'` + `I18n.backend.class.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks)` in a runtime initializer activates fallbacks in every environment including test and development, where fallbacks were previously disabled (the diff removes `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` only from production.rb, profile.rb, and cloud production.rb, so no test-env fallback activation existed before). In specs, a lookup for a key missing in a non-English locale now silently returns the English fallback text where it previously returned the `translation missing: ...` marker (and failed any assertion on exact localized copy). Missing-translation regressions in locale files other than :en become invisible to the suite — the test signal this PR's own feature depends on (fallbacks compensating for incomplete locales) is never exercised by a failing case, and existing specs that assert localized strings in switched locales now pass against English fallback text rather than the locale's real translations.

[ADVISORY] The new `ensure_loaded!` re-implements the exact guard already inlined in `translate` one method below (`load_locale(config.locale) unless @loaded_locales.include?(config.locale)`), leaving the same load-accounting logic maintained in two forms in the same module. The next change to locale-load accounting (e.g., normalizing @loaded_locales entries, adding thread-safety, or changing the memoization) must be replicated in both `translate` and `ensure_loaded!`; if only one is updated, the two entry points into `load_locale` diverge and one path silently skips or double-loads a locale. `translate` could simply call `ensure_loaded!(config.locale)`, deleting the duplicated branch.

goldens.comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).
